question.text: A polysaccharide '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math>' on boiling with dil <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>393</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> under <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>atm</mi></math> pressure yields '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></math>' '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></math>' on treatment with bromine water gives gluconic acid. '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math>' contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">β</mi></math>-glycosidic linkages only. Compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math>' is :

solution.text: Cellulose, C6H10O5n
